description:
FILED s473t2 (Opus triage of the 152 causeless blessed sweep rows), on main 0d783d24.
Probe scratch/s473t2/probes/p11-misc.pl B and C.
Named as a #964-class candidate in docs/blessed-fails-review-s464.md §4c item 1;
this is its probe and its owner.

ROWS BEHIND IT: perl-tests/aassign.t 176 ("undef as lvalue"), 180, 181
("RT #130132 scalar derefffed 1/2"), 182, 183 ("RT #130132 scalar undef 1/2")
= 5 rows.

PROBE (a) -- LHS lvalues are resolved BEFORE any assignment (RT #130132):
    my $x = 1; my $sref = \$x;
    ($sref, $$sref) = (2, 3);
    print "sref=[$sref] x=[$x]";
  perl: sref=[2] x=[3]      PCL: sref=[3] x=[1]
PCL assigns left to right, so `$$sref` is dereferenced AFTER `$sref` has become
2 -- the write lands somewhere else entirely and $x keeps its old value.  With a
short RHS (`($sref, $$sref) = (2)`) perl leaves $x undef; PCL leaves it 1 and
gives $sref 1 (rows 182/183).

PROBE (b) -- `undef` on the LHS uses the RHS element as the lvalue:
    my ($p,$q,$z) = (0,10,20);
    $_++ for ((undef, $p) = ($q, $z));
    print "[$p:$q:$z]";
  perl: 21:11:20            PCL: 21:10:20
The list assignment's result list must contain the RHS element that the `undef`
slot consumed, as an lvalue; PCL returns a copy, so `$q` is not incremented.

Both are the ordering/aliasing contract of aassign; adjacent to round 21's
return protocol (#964) and to the s464 §4c list.
subject: BUG: a list assignment does not resolve its LHS lvalues before assigning, and `undef` on the LHS does not make the RHS element the lvalue (perl-tests/aassign.t, 5 blessed rows -- s464 review §4c item 1, now probed)
